metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:context_sensitivity: At most 64 eligible rows from the first two cached training batches. Each row has at least three real inputs and distinct nonzero latest positive/negative targets. Remove k events from either prefix or suffix, with k uniform in 1..n-2 using a dedicated seed-42 RNG. Both interventions retain the original latest target and identical two-item candidate pool. Margin deltas are perturbed minus full-context positive-negative margins; rank deltas are changes in zero-based positive rank among those two items (positive wins ties), so positive rank deltas mean deterioration. Feature cosines measure sensitivity, not usefulness. Length and removed means describe sampled input and removal event counts; length strata use original input lengths. Suffix removal also increases the event gap to the fixed target, so it is not a pure forgetting control. Padding error is the maximum absolute final-feature difference for identical chronological real inputs under different padding: compare original padded rows against compacted real inputs; for full-length rows, compare against one added leading zero. Measurements use eval mode. padding_check_passed reports whether the maximum error is at most the declared absolute tolerance of 1e-5; this is a numerical diagnostic, not a proof of recurrence correctness. Failure confounds context deltas with padding-induced state changes. Null denotes no eligible measurements. Timestamp gap strata are unavailable because loader batches do not include timestamps. These are conditional training diagnostics, not HR@10, unseen full-catalog ranks, or evidence that cropped training improves validation. No model scores are fused.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:embedding_collapse_score: Mean off-diagonal cosine similarity of up to 2048 real item embeddings, mapped from [-1,1] to [0,1]. About 0.5 corresponds to zero mean cosine; values approaching 1 indicate directional alignment. This does not measure recommendation diversity or unobserved simulator traits. Null means insufficient pairs.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_mean: Mean of (pos_logit - neg_logit) over valid positions; higher means clearer separation.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_p10: 10th percentile of (pos_logit - neg_logit); lower suggests many hard/confusing cases.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate: Fraction where neg_logit > pos_logit (margin < 0); lower is better.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_small_margin_rate: Fraction where (pos_logit - neg_logit) < eps; higher means weak separation.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_category_br: Contains measured valid-position, low-margin and wrong-rank counts with eps=0.5. Valid positions require nonzero input, positive and negative IDs. Category breakdowns are null because item categories are unavailable. All margin metrics are null when no valid samples exist. These are sampled training margins, not validation HR@10 or a full-catalog ranking measurement.
